## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `session-budget-allocation`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-25T06:21:11.864Z.

(27) Session-level budget allocation across turns. Budgets are currently declared per command, which optimises each call in isolation and systematically misallocates across a session: orientation is worth far more at turn one than at turn forty, yet both are charged the same ceiling. Model the session as a sequential allocation problem - a total attention budget spread over an unknown number of remaining turns - and solve it with a simple index policy: spend proportionally more where the expected reduction in the agent's uncertainty is largest, which empirically means front-loading orientation, spending near-zero on repeat orientation when the delta is empty, and reserving a reserve tranche for the deep-context call that a hard problem eventually demands. This composes with (18) rather than competing with it: (18) decides how to degrade within one call once time or tokens run short, while (27) decides how much that call should have been allowed to spend in the first place. It also makes the delta projection work economically visible, because an empty delta should cost near nothing and free budget for later turns.

Sequencing: (25) is implementable immediately against the existing packer and is the cheapest measurable win; (24) needs the intent posterior that (19) already implies but does not expose; (26) is gated on the derived read index and the fleet-allocation primitive; (27) needs per-command budgets to exist first. None of the four requires the cognitive-memory ADR to be accepted - they are engine machinery, not memory subsystems, so no candidate items are filed on that ADR for them.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
